extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a 1.2 million example open-source dataset for training reasoning models, covering math (850K), code (250K), and science (100K) domains. It is built through a systematic pipeline involving question sourcing, mixing, filtering, deduplication, multiple answer sampling per question, and teacher model selection (QwQ-32B). The dataset is designed for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of reasoning models.

extraction.citeAs: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, et al. Data Recipes for Reasoning Models. arXiv:2506.04178, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions are sourced from existing datasets (non-synthetic), semi-synthetic sources (LLM-augmented from existing corpora), and fully synthetic sources (LLM-generated). Answers (reasoning traces) are generated by a teacher model (QwQ-32B) sampling 16 responses per question. The pipeline includes question sourcing, mixing, filtering, deduplication, multiple answer sampling, and optional answer filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from existing datasets including StackExchange CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, OpenMath-2-Math, NuminaMath-1.5, StackExchange Physics, Organic Chemistry PDFs, and many others. Answers (reasoning traces) generated by QwQ-32B teacher model.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For sources that produce fewer datapoints, questions are repeated until the desired amount is reached. Multiple answers (16x) are sampled per question from the teacher model. Exact deduplication is applied for math and science; no deduplication for code.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Pipeline steps include: (1) question sourcing from 27 code, 21 math, and 14 science sources; (2) mixing top-performing sources (top 1-2); (3) question filtering using LLM-based difficulty or response length selection; (4) deduplication (exact match for math/science, none for code); (5) generating 16 answers per question with QwQ-32B; (6) no answer filtering applied. Decontamination against evaluation benchmarks using Indel similarity (75% threshold) and N-gram similarity (N=13).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Answers (reasoning traces) are generated by QwQ-32B as the teacher model, sampling 16 responses per question. No answer filtering is applied in the final pipeline. For question filtering, GPT-4o-mini or GPT-4.1-mini is used to assess difficulty or generate responses for length-based selection.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Experiments showed that no answer filtering strategy (majority consensus, GPT verification, length-based, fastText) outperformed training on all samples without filtering. For question filtering, LLM-based methods (difficulty scoring, response length) outperformed classical methods (fastText, embedding-based).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: QwQ-32B (teacher model for answer generation), GPT-4o-mini (question difficulty filtering, question filtering, answer filtering), GPT-4.1-mini (response length filtering for math and science), GPT-4.1-nano (response length filtering), gemini/gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 (OCR for PDF extraction), FastText (classifier for question and answer filtering)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released on Hugging Face. The OpenThoughts project has gone through multiple generations (BespokeStratos-17K, OpenThoughts-114K, OpenThoughts2-1M, OpenThoughts3-1.2M), suggesting iterative releases. Code is released on GitHub.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Supervised fine-tuning on reasoning data inadvertently degrades the pre-existing safety alignment of base models, increasing harmfulness rates. The paper notes a trade-off between reasoning capabilities and safety.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Distilled reasoning models show generalization deficits, exhibiting strong performance fluctuations across reasoning-invariant problem variations (Alice in Wonderland evaluation). The dataset focuses on math, code, and science, and does not cover reinforcement learning datasets or other domains.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset focuses only on SFT data for math, code, and science reasoning. It does not cover RL training data, staged SFT, or curriculum learning. The dataset may not generalize well to other domains. Safety alignment is degraded by training on this data without explicit safety tuning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of reasoning models for math, code, and science domains. The dataset is intended for training small to mid-scale language models to develop long chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities.

inLanguage.evidence: Removing Non-English Answers: Ask GPT-4o-mini whether a provided answer contains only English.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We can broadly categorize our question sourcing techniques into three types: (1) Fully synthetic – an existing LLM generates questions with little-to-no seed material... (2) Semi-synthetic – an LLM uses existing data sources such as CommonCrawl or FineWeb as seeds to form questions... (3) Non-synthetic – humans write the questions.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Our experiments cover 27 different question sources for code questions, 21 sources for math, and 14 sources for science... Non-synthetic – humans write the questions. Examples include StackExchange and ShareGPTCode. These questions often arise from online forums, contests, chatbot interactions, and other sources.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Our experiments cover 27 different question sources for code questions, 21 sources for math, and 14 sources for science... Takeaway: We use OpenMath-2-Math as our sole math question source, CodeGolf and OpenCodeReasoning as our code question sources, and StackExchangePhysics and OrganicChemistryPDFs as our science question sources... Takeaway: We use QwQ-32B as the teacher model.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: For sources that produce fewer datapoints, we repeat the questions until we reach the desired amount... Our final pipeline uses 16× answers per question for all domains. It uses exact deduplication for math and science and no deduplication for code.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We investigate (1) sourcing questions from existing and newly generated datasets, (2) mixing questions from the top-performing sources, (3) filtering for high-quality questions using fastText or LLMs, (4) deduplicating questions and sampling multiple answers per question, (5) filtering out low-quality answers using LLM verification or majority consensus, and (6) selecting the best teacher model... we perform decontamination against our evaluation sets, via two separate criteria.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Takeaway: We use QwQ-32B as the teacher model... Our final pipeline uses 16× answers per question for all domains... Takeaway: We do not perform answer filtering because no filtering strategy outperformed the baseline, which uses all the answers.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: For math datasets, the random filtering baseline outperformed all other filtering methods... across all domains, the no-filtering strategy (training on all samples without controlling compute) led to performance similar to that of all other methods of filtering... For all domains, using LLM-based filtering methods outperformed classical filtering methods such as embedding-based and fastText filters.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Our final pipeline uses 16× answers per question for all domains.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We use QwQ-32B as the teacher model... We use difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini for code questions, and response length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini for math and science questions... We use GPT-4o-mini for all sources that we generate which require an LLM... We use gemini/gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 with the prompt in Figure 24 to extract the text from the PDFs.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We release our model and our dataset as part of a collection on Hugging Face. Our OpenThinker3-7B model can be found in https://huggingface.co/open-thoughts/OpenThinker3-7B, and our dataset can be found in https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts3-1.2M. Our codebase will be released at https://github.com/open-thoughts/open-thoughts.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: we observe that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning inadvertently degrades the pre-existing safety alignment of Qwen2.5 models, consistent with prior findings Qi et al. (2023)... OpenThinker3-7B was trained without any explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data, which likely contributes to its degraded safety performance... These findings underscore the challenge of balancing safety and utility in reasoning models.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Distilled reasoning models, while strongly improving over standard LLMs, still suffer from generalization deficits, as evident from strong performance fluctuations across natural problem and solution structure preserving variations in problem templates... We did not explore datasets for reinforcement learning, a standard training regime for building reasoning models.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We did not explore datasets for reinforcement learning, a standard training regime for building reasoning models. Within the SFT realm, we did not explore the use of staged SFT or curriculum learning to further improve performance... OpenThinker3-7B was trained without any explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data, which likely contributes to its degraded safety performance.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The goal of the OpenThoughts project is to create open-source datasets for training reasoning models... Our goal is to create the best dataset of question-response pairs for SFT reasoning... fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on it to yield OpenThinker3-7B.
